gaps.criterion: MFA and SSO paths both reach an authenticated session
gaps.gap: NEITHER PATH CAN REACH A SESSION, because there is nothing to reach. Both depend on ProjexCloud sdk-identity - POST /api/mfa/challenge and /verify for the second factor, and the SSO redirect plus GET /api/userinfo for the federated path - and no issuer is reachable in this environment: PROJEXCLOUD_IDENTITY_URL is unset, the gateway is unconfigured, and the Verdaccio registry is down. What ships is the CLIENT half: MfaChallenge takes onVerify and onResend callbacks and drives the full interaction, with the code shape, formatting, leading-zero handling and failure behaviour asserted by 16 unit tests. It is not wired to a live challenge because there is no endpoint to wire it to, and the SSO redirect screen is not built at all rather than built against a guessed contract - the redirect target, state parameter and callback shape are the issuer's to define, and inventing them would produce code that looks finished and matches nothing. This closes when an sdk-identity instance exists: the same task should wire MfaChallenge to the real challenge/verify pair, add the SSO redirect and callback screens, and prove both with a Gherkin scenario that ends signed in.

gaps.criterion: Keyboard-only completion of every auth flow
gaps.gap: Built for it throughout and reasoned about explicitly, but not PROVEN by an executable artifact. Every control is a real focusable element: each step of the wizard is a genuine form whose submit advances it, so Enter moves forward from any field; Back and Send-a-new-code are <button type=button> rather than links with click handlers, so both Enter and Space activate them; the MFA field is deliberately ONE input rather than the mockup's six boxes, which would be a keyboard trap needing bespoke arrow, paste and backspace handling and would announce six unlabelled fields; autofocus lands on the first field of each step; and the step counter is aria-live so a change is announced rather than silently swapping under a keyboard user whose focus has not moved. None of that is asserted by a runner. The unit tests cover the logic beneath the screens, not focus order or tab traversal, and a real keyboard walk needs the Playwright/BDD runner, which cannot currently reach tests/features - the Test MCP container has no LeadFlow workspace mount. Closing this means a Gherkin scenario completing sign-in, MFA and signup using only navigate, fill, press and click steps, executed green.
